#3052. Retiring Before Age 65 in 2027? 2 Key Things You Need to Know

There are some crucial things to be aware of if your retirement is happening before the midpoint of your 60s.

Though some people might choose to wait until age 65 to bring their careers to an end, there's absolutely no rule stating you have to do the same. And if you've saved well and are ready for that next stage of life, there's nothing wrong with retiring before age 65.

If that's what you're gearing up for in 2027, it's important to go in prepared. Here are two key things to know.

Many people's health insurance is tied to their jobs. If you retire at 65, you'll generally be eligible to enroll in Medicare. If you'll be younger when you retire, you'll need a plan to secure health coverage.

Now you may be thinking you can get by without insurance for a few months if that's all it takes to bridge the gap until Medicare kicks in. But remember, all it takes is a single medical emergency without insurance to upend your finances and destroy your savings.

If you have good coverage through your current job, you might consider continuing it through COBRA if you're close to 65. With COBRA, you pay your premiums for your workplace plan without an employer subsidy, but you also get to retain the coverage you're familiar with.

If you're at least 62 when you retire, you'll be able to sign up for Social Security. But you won't be eligible to collect your monthly benefits in full.

That won't happen until age 67, which is your Social Security full retirement age. For each month you file before full retirement age, your benefits are permanently reduced.

Smaller Social Security checks may not be a problem for you if you have a lot of savings and can afford to receive less money each month. But if you don't want to reduce your benefits, you'll need to make sure your savings can sustain you once you leave your job.

Of course, there's another option. You could retire from your current job but work part-time in a role or field you enjoy. That could give you more free time without the same strain on your retirement account.

A 2027 retirement is an exciting thing to look forward to. But if you won't be 65 at the time you end your career, there are special considerations to think about. Make sure you've explored health insurance options and understand when to claim Social Security so your retirement finances aren't thrown for a loop.

#3050. Sysco Corp (SYY) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Sysco met earnings targets amid weaker restaurant traffic and an AI push.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Sysco Corporation (SYY -9.33%) reported first quarter financial results that met earnings expectations despite macroeconomic pressures including restaurant traffic declines and food cost deflation. Management emphasized a three-part strategy focused on core business performance, an AI-driven tech transformation targeting significant cost savings, and the integration of the pending Jetro Restaurant Depot acquisition. The company reaffirmed its full-year adjusted earnings guidance while adjusting its top-line outlook to reflect lower inflationary trends in the food distribution sector.

Operator: Welcome to Sysco's first quarter fiscal year 2027 conference call. As a reminder, today's call is being recorded. We will begin with opening remarks and introductions. I would like to turn the call over to Kevin Kim, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Kevin Kim: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Sysco's first quarter fiscal year 2027 earnings call. On today's call, we have Kevin Hourican, our Chair of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, and Brandon Sewell, our Chief Financial Officer. Before we begin, please note that statements made during this presentation that state the company's or management's intentions, beliefs, expectations, or predictions of the future are forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, and actual results could differ in a material manner. Additional information about factors that could cause results to differ from those in the forward-looking statements is contained in the company's SEC filings.

This includes, but is not limited to, risk factors contained in our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended June 27, 2026, subsequent SEC filings, and in the news release issued earlier this morning. A copy of these materials can be found in the Investor section at sysco.com. Non-GAAP financial measures are included in our comments today and in our presentation slides. The reconciliation of those non-GAAP measures to the corresponding GAAP measures is included at the end of the presentation slides, can also be found in the Investor section of our website. During the discussion today, unless otherwise stated, all results are compared to the same quarter in the prior year.

To ensure we have sufficient time to answer all questions, we would like to ask each participant to limit their time today to one question. If you have a follow-up question, we ask that you re-enter the queue. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Kevin Hourican.

Kevin Hourican: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Sysco's Q1 fiscal year 2027 earnings call. This is a pivotal moment in Sysco's ongoing journey of growth, resilience, and operational excellence. Our leadership team is focused on three major activities this year. First, delivering with excellence for our customers, as well as our core Sysco financial commitments, including the planned acceleration in profit growth on a year-over-year basis. Second, improving our operating margins through an AI-powered business transformation. Third, preparing for the anticipated closure of the Jetro Restaurant Depot transaction by the third quarter of this fiscal year. Each of these critical priorities is on track, and I would like to discuss each of them during our call this morning.

Let's start with chapter one, our core business. Sysco delivered a strong first quarter of fiscal 2027. We delivered adjusted earnings per share of $1.19, meeting our expectations. We delivered earnings growth in the quarter despite ongoing softness in restaurant foot traffic, rising fuel costs, and U.S. food cost deflation in the period. The last two of these three factors performed differently than we had planned for the quarter. Importantly, Sysco delivered our earnings guidance for the quarter despite these headwinds. I am proud of the team for their agility and decisive action.

As seen on slide seven, during the quarter, we grew our local case volume +2.7%, slightly higher than we had planned, representing a 130 basis point step-up on a two-year stack basis sequentially versus Q4. Our local business is building positive momentum, and we are growing our share. Enterprise sales reached $21.7 billion, up 2.8% year-over-year, despite enterprise inflation coming in at only positive 0.3%. The lower-than-expected food cost inflation accounts for the sales delta in the period versus our expectations. That said, we measure our business health via profitable volume growth, and we are encouraged by our team's strong execution in achieving our volume objectives during the quarter.

I would like to highlight a few items within the macroeconomic environment before I dive a bit deeper into our performance. Traffic to restaurants per Black Box Intelligence was down 2% in the quarter. The traffic performance for the quarter is consistent with the calendar year-to-date performance and remains a headwind for the industry. Additionally, the Cyclospora outbreak had an adverse impact on the middle of the quarter, softening traffic to restaurants and restaurant operator volume during August. Sysco specifically had stronger volume performance in July and September, as customers bounced back quickly after the Cyclospora traffic headwind. The 2.7% volume growth for Q1 is inclusive of the Cyclospora headwind, showcasing the underlying momentum of our local case volume growth.

Rising fuel costs are impacting supply chains and end customers. As we mentioned on our Q4 earnings call, inbound logistics costs have risen due to the continued increase in diesel fuel. Brandon will discuss these dynamics during his section of our call today. Our team has done an excellent job of hedging fuel costs on the outbound delivery aspect of our business, but the rising cost of fuel is harmful to end consumer disposable income. Sysco is being thoughtful about the decisions that we are making on the fuel headwind to ensure we keep food affordable for our customers.

We will revisit these decisions regularly to ensure we are managing our P&L and our relative price competitiveness in the end market. Lastly, food cost inflation came in lower than planned during the quarter, as seen on slide eight. Our enterprise inflation was +0.3%, and our USFS business was deflationary for the period. As you know, we budgeted inflation at approximately positive 1.5%-2% for the year. The deflation of food in Q1 was helpful for end consumers, but creates some short-term pressure on our P&L. Our merchants did an excellent job in the quarter of ensuring highly competitive procurement costs inbound to Sysco, and our revenue management teams ensured that product deflation was properly priced to our end customers.

Given Q1 was deflationary in the U.S., we now expect for our overall basket of goods to increase sub-1% inflation in Q2 and approximately 1%-1.5% for the full year based on commodity input cost projections. Sysco grew our business profitably in the quarter within the business conditions that I just described. The 2.7% local case growth speaks to the improving selling capabilities of our sales consultants and the improved productivity they are delivering. Both retention and tenure of our sales consultants remain strong, and the effectiveness of our AI360 selling tool continues to improve. Our sales consultants who use the selling tool more often are selling more to their customers.

As a result, those SCs are making more money than their peers. Our sales leadership team continues to coach to the effectiveness of selling with and through AI360, and our technology team continues to bring new capabilities to the tool. Regarding gross margins, we expanded our gross margin year-over-year by 18 basis points. The strong margin performance is due to strengthening customer mix and a step-up in our Sysco Brand performance. Specific to Sysco Brand, we grew our mix by 44 basis points year-over-year in local, and we were positive in total USBL Sysco Brand mix for the first time in many quarters.

We are making progress in Sysco Brand in all customer types, restaurants of all sizes, as well as our non-commercial segment. Encouragingly, the greatest progress is being made with our local street customers. The work our merchants have done to expand our value tier assortment within Sysco Brand is making a difference, and our sales teams are doing an increasingly good job of offering Sysco Brand savings to our customers. We expect this positive momentum to continue in 2027. As it relates to our expenses, our supply chain performed at a high level during the first quarter. We delivered on our plan in logistics cost per piece, and we have improved our on-time performance versus our delivery windows.

Strong supply chain performance was partially offset by higher fuel costs and medical expenses. Brandon will touch on these topics in more detail. As previously outlined, we expect our operating margins to expand throughout the year as the majority of our AI and tech transformation benefit will be realized during the second half. Lastly, our international segment posted another strong quarter with adjusted operating income growth of 12.2%, marking our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted profit growth. Our international team grew local cases 3.2% and posted strong Sysco Brand growth. Chapter two on our call today is an update on our AI-powered business transformation.

Recently, we announced an AI and tech-powered business transformation program that we expect will unlock $100 million of net cost savings in fiscal 2027 and $500 million of net cost savings by the close of fiscal 2029. This work directly supports the updated midterm financial targets that we recently shared for fiscals 2028 and 2029, which included 4%-7% sales growth, 9%-11% adjusted EPS growth, and 12%-14% total shareholder return. I would like to provide a quick update on the early innings of these efforts. The transformation program currently consists of 30 initiatives across the enterprise, with four of those initiatives driving approximately 70% of the total value, as you can see on slide 11.

The Q1 impact of these efforts met our expectations, and the value delivery significantly ramps into the second half of fiscal 2027. We have launched our routing project, which is the largest individual contributor to improved service levels at a lower operating cost. The routing initiative is now live in pilot regions and is delivering 2%-4% improvement in pieces per mile driven and increasing compliance to our on-time delivery windows to our customers. This is phase one of the project, and we plan to roll out the improved routing capability across all Sysco U.S. operating locations this year.

Every 1% improvement in pieces per mile delivers approximately $3 million of efficiency gains once scaled across the organization beyond this initial pilot. Phase two of the project is focused on further enhancing the improved routing capability with AI-infused flexibility and dynamic modeling. We expect to see an additional reduction to miles driven and a service improvement with the second phase of the work. Phase two is expected to begin in the second half of fiscal year 2027 and run through fiscal year 2028. The goal is clear: improve service while lowering cost. This project is especially important given today's high-cost fuel environment.

After we have completed the rollout across our U.S. broadline business, we plan to expand the capability to our specialty and international business units. I would like to voice a special thank you to our transportation team for their hard work. A second example today is within our indirect sourcing function. We launched our first AI-powered RFP in recent weeks. The tool performed as expected, rapidly completing the RFP autonomously with a human in the loop supervising the process. The results of the RFP exceeded our procurement savings target by approximately 30%.

As Brandon has explained, the power of this capability is not only to source existing categories more effectively, but also the ability for us to RFP smaller categories of spend that would not historically warrant dedicated resources. The objectives are to cover more spend with RFPs and increase our savings percentages. We have been asked several times lately if the AI technology capabilities that we are building can be applied to Restaurant Depot post-close. The short answer is yes, and this indirect sourcing project is a great example. Lastly, I'd like to provide an update on our AI selling tools. Our AI360 sales consultant enablement tool continues to gain traction. We measure success in two simple ways.

One, are we presenting sales offers to more customers? This is an activity measure. And two, are we selling more products to existing customers? This is an outcome measure. I am pleased to report that both the activity level and the outcome metrics have increased through the use of AI360. More customer visits have a pitched sales opportunity, and more customers are saying yes to those sales offers more often. The why is the tool itself. It prioritizes for SCs what to focus on any given sales call. The tool suggests items to sell or items to convert to Sysco Brand. The decisions are still 100% in the hands of our SC.

SCs that are new to the company and SCs that have decades of experience benefit from the sales suggestions. The power is in the data. As I mentioned a moment ago, we are building momentum and gaining traction on Sysco Brand conversion and penetration. This is a direct result of the AI360 tool prompting and prioritizing that sales activity. Most importantly, our colleagues are making more money as a result of these selling activities, which becomes the self-fulfilling flywheel of the tool utilization. Chapter three of our call today is an update on the Jetro Restaurant Depot transaction. The government review process continues to proceed as expected.

Sysco and Restaurant Depot have substantially completed our respective responses to the FTC's second request. We expect the deal to be approved, and we remain on target to close the transaction by the end of Sysco's fiscal Q3. I would also like to provide an update on the performance results from Jetro Restaurant Depot. We have been advised by their leadership that the most recently completed quarter, 1% volume growth supported operating profit and EBITDA increases year over year, both on a dollar and a margin basis. Restaurant Depot experienced 1.6% product deflation within the period.

Year to date on a calendar year basis, Jetro Restaurant Depot is delivering compelling overall financial performance with sales and profit growth versus prior year. Ahead of deal closure, our integration teams are hard at work on planning for day one as a combined company. Playbooks are being built to unlock the capability of buying together, reducing our food costs, and supporting our ability to buy better to sell better. By being more efficient in our buying activity, we can strengthen our P&L and provide more value to more customers through Sysco delivery and Jetro Restaurant Depot store locations. We have also begun the planning activities for the better together customer engagement opportunities that we believe can create revenue upside.

We have a clear line of sight for how we can create value for additional customers, providing them better service at affordable prices across more communities. These revenue synergy opportunities are being thoughtfully planned, sized, and we will communicate our projections at an investor day post-close. Morale is high at both companies, and the collective teams are excited to get to work post-deal approval. In summary today, Sysco is poised to unlock greater shareholder value by delivering the following three outcomes: a strong core Sysco, as evidenced by our Q1 results, a more efficient Sysco future through AI transformation, and post-close, a combined new company that we expect will grow faster and be more profitable than a standalone Sysco.

These three forces, when working together, give our board, management, and global colleagues confidence in our future. We are strengthening the foundation of the company and building future capabilities that will differentiate Sysco from the rest of the industry. Our customers and colleagues will benefit from the actions we are taking, and our shareholders will be the net beneficiaries of the profitable market share we can capture. We are excited for our future. With that, I'd now like to turn the call over to Brandon, who will walk through his perspectives on our financial performance. Brandon, over to you.

Brandon Sewell: Thank you, Kevin, and good morning, everyone. We appreciate your time. Today, we will provide an update on Sysco's Q1 financial performance, review the successful September financing for JRD, and reaffirm our adjusted EPS outlook, including the company-wide actions underway to accelerate top-line sales growth, deliver on our $100 million cost savings program, further support margin management, and importantly, accelerating adjusted EPS growth for the remainder of the year. Consistent with the commitments we previously outlined, our teams delivered 2.7% local growth in our U.S. foodservice segment and effectively managed margins despite the deflationary environment. This performance drove adjusted EPS of $1.19, in line with our expectations and 3.5% higher year-over-year.

Despite the macroeconomic and industry challenges Kevin outlined, our company-specific initiatives kept us focused on the elements of performance within our control in a choppy operating environment. As shown on slide 13, Q1 sales grew 2.8%, driven by balanced volume growth across USFS local and national accounts, and continued outsized growth in our international segment. Enterprise inflation was only 0.3% during the quarter, below consensus expectations of 1.5%, and included 0.3% deflation in our US broadline operations. Strong margin management expanded gross margin, drove enterprise adjusted operating income growth, and marked another quarter of adjusted operating income growth in our USFS segment.

Next, we successfully completed the bond and equity financing for the cash component of the JRD transaction, reflecting strong execution, robust investor demand, and attractive pricing. Consistent with the plan we outlined earlier in March, we raised $11.75 billion through senior notes, $5 billion through hybrid debt, and $1 billion through equity. Combined with $3.75 billion of committed term loans and approximately $200 million of commercial paper, these actions position us well for the pending close. Inclusive of more than $300 million of interest rate hedging proceeds, our effective cost of debt was 5.8%, providing attractive long-term financing for Sysco.

This outcome demonstrates the strength of our investment-grade credit profile, our commitment to deleveraging and maintaining our mid-triple B credit rating, and investor confidence in our strategic direction. This is a strong outcome for Sysco and our shareholders. Our team's preparation enabled us to execute within a relatively narrow window of opportunity in September. We remain confident in our net cost savings targets, $100 million in FY 2027, with benefits accelerating in the second half, and $500 million by FY 2029. As Kevin noted, based on current visibility, four key projects represent approximately 70% of the program's expected value. Indirect spend management is one of those projects within finance. Given Sysco's size and scale, these new agentic reverse auction technology tools can improve transparency, reduce value leakage, and optimize over $1 billion of annual indirect spend. We recently piloted the tool for truck parts and tires, with additional events planned in the near term.

Momentum is building, and we expect continued progress with real-time negotiations and secure value from suppliers, with the goal of supporting our deleveraging commitments. This is a tangible example of how Sysco-specific initiatives can improve financial performance. These are net cost savings that we expect to flow to the bottom line, particularly in the second half. The opportunity becomes even more compelling when combined with gross margin expansion from local volume growth and increased Sysco Brand penetration. Our supply chain also continues to deliver compounding productivity gains driven by retention, a trend we expect to continue over the coming year. Collectively, these efforts give us visibility into accelerating top and bottom line growth for the remainder of the year.

I will return to this point shortly. Now let's review our quarterly performance and its key financial drivers, beginning on slide 13. For the first quarter, enterprise sales grew 2.8% on an as-reported basis, driven by U.S. Foodservice, international, and SYGMA. Total U.S. Foodservice volume increased 2.6%, and local volume increased 2.7% in the quarter. In USFS local, performance exceeded our guidance range and represented a 130 basis point sequential improvement on a two-year stacked basis. Deflation in USBL was approximately 0.3%. International inflation was approximately 0.8% on a constant currency basis. Based on current visibility, we expect inflation to increase over the course of the year in both our U.S. operations and the enterprise overall.

During the quarter, elevated fuel costs continued to affect food input costs and inbound transportation expense. Even so, Sysco continues to manage the industry's fuel-related challenges effectively and remains in a strong relative position, with approximately 80% of our bulk fuel purchases hedged over the next fiscal year. In the first quarter, Sysco generated $4.1 billion of gross profit, up 3.8%, and expanded gross margin by 18 basis points to 18.6%, while improving gross profit per case. The improvement in gross profit reflected local volume growth, customer fuel surcharges, increased Sysco Brand penetration, savings from strategic sourcing initiatives, and tariff benefits. Adjusted operating expenses were $3.1 billion for the quarter, up 4% and equal to 14.4% of sales.

The increase reflected planned investments in higher growth areas of the business, along with an increase in fuel costs. Corporate adjusted expenses increased 4.8% from the prior year, primarily reflecting higher insurance and benefits costs, partially offset by productivity savings and corporate efficiencies. Sequential volume improvements also benefited USFS, our largest business segment, which delivered another quarter of improving financial performance. International delivered 5.1% sales growth and 12.2% adjusted operating income growth, marking its 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted profit growth.

SYGMA results moderated in the quarter with sales growth of 1% and lower operating income. Against a challenging fuel backdrop, the SYGMA team remains focused on capturing operating efficiencies. For the quarter, adjusted EBITDA was $1.1 billion, up 5.4% from the prior year. Let's now turn to the balance sheet and cash flow. Our investment-grade balance sheet remains strong and reflects a healthy financial profile. We ended the quarter with a 2.4x net debt leverage ratio and $5.8 billion in total liquidity, well above our minimum threshold and providing meaningful financial flexibility. Turning to cash flow, we generated approximately $278 million in operating cash flow, up more than 220%.

Free cash flow was $+230 million, reflecting timing of working capital, an increase in adjusted EBITDA, and the timing of CapEx. Now, let me review our expectations for FY 2027, as shown on slide 20. Consistent with the guidance provided on our last earnings call, we expect continued volume growth and an acceleration in adjusted EPS growth. All elements of our fiscal 2027 guidance reflect standalone Sysco and include the 53rd week. For FY 2027, we continue to expect full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS growth of 9%-11%, with our outlook centered on approximately 10% adjusted EPS growth for the year. We remain committed to the delivery of $100 million of in-year net cost savings, as detailed on slide 11.

While fuel expenses remain elevated, recall that in Q1 and throughout the year, our increases in operating expenses are generally offset by increases in gross profit via customer surcharges. We are well-positioned throughout the remainder of the year. We now expect reported net sales growth to be at the lower end of our prior 6%-7% range, reflecting a lower inflationary environment for the industry. We are reiterating our USFS local case volume growth guidance of approximately 2.5% for the year, and the 53rd week contributes approximately 2% of reported growth. Based on the current outlook, we expect inflation of approximately 1%-1.5%.

We expect cost-saving benefits to build throughout the year, with the largest contribution expected in the second half and a corresponding acceleration in profit growth. We remain on track to return approximately $1 billion to shareholders through dividends. We also continue to expect adjusted depreciation and amortization of approximately $850 million for the year. As a reminder, Q4 includes an extra week this year. We now expect interest expense of $680 million, other expense of $20 million, and a weighted average share count of approximately 487 million shares for the year to account for the September equity raise and current interest rate environment. Looking ahead, our teams remain focused on sustaining positive momentum through fiscal 2027.

We remain excited about the pending JRD transaction, which represents a significant next chapter of growth and will create a preeminent multichannel foodservice distribution platform. Combining the momentum in standalone Sysco with JRD will strengthen our financial profile and support long-term shareholder value creation. With that, I will turn the call back to Kevin for closing remarks.

Kevin Hourican: Thank you, Brandon. In closing out today's call, I am pleased to announce that Brandon has been named Sysco's next Chief Financial Officer. We conducted a thorough global search for our next CFO, and our Board was unanimous that Brandon was the best choice. Brandon has distinguished himself as a trusted and highly effective leader throughout his 12 years with the company, and when asked to step in as Interim Chief Financial Officer, he performed at a high level. Brandon commands a deep knowledge of our business, broad financial expertise, and strong understanding of how Sysco creates shareholder value.

We are pleased with the strong performance that we have delivered in Q1, and more importantly, the significant progress that we are making as a company across sales, merchandising, and operations. I want to thank our 75,000 Sysco colleagues for the strong start to the year. Their collective hard work, dedication, and execution have positioned Sysco well to deliver on our 2027 plan. With that, Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator: Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, press star one on your keypad. To leave the queue at any time, press star two. Once again, that is star one to ask a question. We will take our first question from Edward Kelly with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Edward Kelly: Yeah, hi. Good morning, guys. Brandon, congratulations on the promotion. I wanted to start on local case volume growth. Could you maybe just provide a bit more color around the impact of Cyclospora that you saw during the quarter, what October looks like, and then as we think about these comparisons as we move through the year, you lose the M&A benefit. So I am curious in terms of your confidence in hitting that 2.5% target as the compares get harder. Then just a quick follow-up on this inflation issue. Obviously softer than expected, and that is a headwind to growing gross profit and earnings. What are you hearing from vendors about the path from here?

I mean, it seems like we are going to see some real re-acceleration, which I would imagine would be good for your business as well as the Restaurant Depot side, given the deflationary level we saw there this quarter.

Kevin Hourican: Good morning, Ed. Thank you for the questions. It's Kevin. I'll start on the volume topic. I'll then bridge into what we see for inflation for the year, toss it over to Brandon, who will help round that out from a quantum perspective. To the very first part of your question, which was Cyclospora, to start with, we're pleased with our first quarter performance, meeting our expectations in spite of these macro conditions that I enumerated on our call. Cyclospora specifically impacted the month of August. We had a stronger July. We had a stronger September.

The Cyclospora headwind that transpired for about six weeks in the middle of the quarter is included in the positive 2.7% volume growth, and I think that's a strong statement of the progress that we're making. Specific to October, I think you have seen some restaurant names reported earlier this week and last week that the start of October was a little bit softer for the industry. We saw a little bit of that too. The good news is that has progressed solidly as the month of October has progressed. Weeks three and four of October stronger, November off to a good start. Not sure exactly what that blip was in the beginning of October.

Perhaps it's midterm election noise, perhaps it's fuel, but as I said, that was a short duration thing relative to October. We're anchoring on our full year guide, the 2.5% volume guide for the year. We are confident in our ability to deliver our profit guidance for this year, given all of what we see and more importantly, what we're working on. The second half steps up from a profit growth perspective because of the AI commitments, and our strategic sourcing activities, as you know, impact the second half of the year more than the first. Let's bridge to this inflation/deflation question. The first quarter did behave differently than we had planned. I can highlight the causals of that.

It's dairy. The categories of dairy was down significantly from a deflation perspective. That's for two reasons. Number one, lapping high inflation a year ago from avian influenza, and then in the fluid dairy milk categories and impacting cheese as well, there was a meaningful oversupply, which was not anticipated. So oversupply brought price down. That's specific to dairy. The second category is in poultry. Poultry is currently significantly deflationary. That too is because of lapping avian influenza from a year ago.

What we can see in our modeling, and I'm going to toss to Brandon, who can talk about Q2 and the rest of the year, is we begin lapping avian influenza in period four for poultry, and we begin lapping it in period six from a dairy perspective. That is impacting, in a constructive way, the rate of inflation that we will see in the second half. The oversupply of milk is something that will be addressed as it relates to how they produce milk, et cetera, because they don't want to see the oversupply extend for an extended period of time.

Brandon, over to you to talk about the year and how we're thinking about inflation now for the rest of the year.

Brandon Sewell: Yeah. Thank you, Ed, and thank you for the congratulations. I do appreciate the support. Let me go back to the first question you had, then I will jump to inflation. Part of your question was, do we see continued improvement as the laps become more difficult? For Q1, the 2.7% local on a two-year stack, it was an improvement versus Q4 of about 130 basis points. We are getting stronger. We see positive momentum and penetration, and the reason for that is because of the tenure of our sales force, which will continue throughout the year. Jumping to inflation, Kevin called it out, we were at 0.3%. Our broad line in the U.S. deflation was 0.3%.

With that, we are lapping avian flu, so in October already, we see just under 1%, so that will continue throughout Q2, and then we see an improvement in Q3 and Q4. We updated our sales guidance due to that inflation, and with that, we managed our margins quite well during the quarter. We had excellent operational cost performance as well in Q1. It is a core competency of ours, and that as well will continue. We are enthused by our bottom line profitability performance and expect that to continue in Q2 and the second half.

Kevin Hourican: Just to be crystal clear, Brandon said for period four, October, approximately 1%, that was positive. Just to be crystal clear, we have already begun to see the lapping of the avian influenza from a year ago, and we expect to be positive for the rest of the year.

Operator: Thank you. We will move next to John Heinbockel with Guggenheim. Please go ahead.

John Heinbockel: Hey, Kevin. Two related things. When you look at AI360, maybe speak to the potential impact there on local cases. Kevin Hourican: Okay, very good. Thank you, John. Two good questions. Start at the AI360 topic. So overall industry cases per operator is down, and our performance is solid. The why is AI360, the power is in the data.

It is prompting to our sales reps things they should be selling that they are not currently selling, or it is predicting that there is the potential risk for a future loss based on rolling 16 weeks data, and it prompts them to take action. We're seeing solid, strong penetration performance, and I directly attribute that to our tenure improvement, retention improvement of our colleagues, which Brandon already covered, and then the leverage of AI360. We absolutely see the performance data that you're implying, John. Your top decile users are performing meaningfully higher than the bottom decile users, and that's across all tenure durations, one-year colleague to 30-year colleague. We can slice the data that way.

Using it more means you make more money as a sales consultant. Using it more means you're profitably growing your business. We've not quantified the impact to this full year's volume performance, but I would say it's what gives me confidence in our ability to deliver our 2.5% volume growth for the full year. As Ed mentioned, that's a step up each quarter because we lap stronger numbers a year ago. AI360 is what's giving us the confidence to do that. We're going to continue to make it better. We launched new capabilities and new tools. The other thing I would point to on AI360 as a direct proof point is our progress in Sysco Brand.

Very pleased with AI360. Shout out to our tech team for that proprietary product development that we have built and our sales colleagues for embracing it. It's a real winner for us. We are seeing product inflation internationally at a higher rate than domestic U.S. That's mostly because of how food is priced and contracted.

In a couple of our countries, it's a twice-per-year government-impacted price negotiation, and that tends to result in a more stubborn price in select countries, and that is one of the reasons why food cost is inflationary in Europe particularly, while deflationary in the U.S. Brandon, over to you for anything you want to add.

Brandon Sewell: Yeah, we've used our U.S. programs as somewhat of an incubation to then transfer to our international, and it's working really well. In the international space, in every region, we delivered 3+% local, and it's a major contributor to the profit growth. As Kevin referenced, we're in our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit operating income growth, and we expect that to continue.

Operator: Thank you. We'll move next to Danilo Gargiulo with Bernstein. Please go ahead. Your line is now open.

Danilo Gargiulo: Great. First of all, Brandon, once again, congratulations on your appointment as permanent CFO. Brandon Sewell: Sure. Thank you for the question and the congratulations, Danilo. I appreciate it. I will start with our core business and OpEx, and then I will move to the topic of fuel. We ended FY 2026 with the highest retention on both selectors and drivers since the beginning of COVID. With that, between, as we stated in the prepared remarks, fuel hedges offset by some of the customer surcharges, the overall impact to operating income of fuel was relatively small. We are being very intentional in managing that pressure between our customers and our internal P&L. We did it in Q1, and we will continue to do it in Q2 and in FY 2027.

The one piece I would remind you of, Danilo, is when we have increased fuel costs, you will see OpEx increase, and you will also see margin increase because of those customer surcharges. It is a geography change in the P&L that occurs.

Operator: Thank you. We will move next to Kelly Bania with BMO Capital. Please go ahead.

Just wondering at what point do retention tailwinds kind of level off and other drivers take over in terms of supporting that figure?

Do you have like a same-store sales type of volume figure on that front? Thank you.

Kevin Hourican: Good morning, Kelly. Thank you for the questions. Going back to Ed's question, yes, we will lap that acquisition come the December period of time. We're confident in our ability to hit the 2.5% for the full year because of a host of strategic initiatives that are in play that will positively impact our local case growth. We are not expecting macro environmental conditions to improve to be able to deliver our performance. It's from strategic initiatives.

Specific to your point on colleague retention, I don't view that as a slowing down tailwind. Brandon makes the point well at our monthly business reviews. Tenure improvement continues on in perpetuity. The person who's one year in today will be two years in tomorrow, will be three years in the year after that, and they continue to get better. So, while we have improved retention, what was temporary was the customer loss impact of that, but will be permanent is the continued strengthening of their selling skills that grows over time. So, our improved retention will continue to be a tailwind throughout 2027. I'm reminded always how much this is a relationship business.

Our restaurants buy food from us at least twice per week, 52 weeks per year. Our sales rep and our driver is in their place of business multiple times per week. It's a really intimate, relationships-based transaction, and the strengthening of the colleague retention and tenure will be a tailwind for all of 2027, and I submit even into 2028. What gives me confidence is, back to John's question, AI360 is not yet fully developed as it relates to what it can do. Colleagues are using it every day, but they can use it even more. We can be even more specific about what we prompt our colleagues on what they focus on.

One of the biggest focuses on the year-to-date for us is actually an increased effort and focus on winning net new business. So you're going to see a big focus from us in that regard to help us grow our customer count, which gives us the confidence in our full year guide. As it relates to RD, just Restaurant Depot, we have not unpacked same store sales versus new store growth.

What I like about RD's performance, they grew their customer count, they grew their transaction count, they improved their profitability year-over-year, including expanding their Op margins. Richard and his team have grown profit for 30 consecutive years, and they are on track to be able to do that again this year. It is a really capable, talented team. Brandon, toss to you for anything you would like to add.

Brandon Sewell: No, I would just reemphasize that last point, 30 out of 30 years. Our conversation with the Restaurant Depot team continue to be very positive, and each time we speak with them and interact with them, we become more impressed. We think that they will make Sysco better, and their track record for profit improvement is perfect, 30 out of 30, and they continue to do that this year.

Kevin Hourican: Just one more proof point, coming back, Kelly, to confidence in our ability on the improved financial performance is Sysco Brand. Our merchant teams, as I said in my prepared remarks, have done a really terrific job of improving our assortment at the value tier end of the equation, AI360, putting those opportunities in front of our sales reps to do the Swap and Save. We improved Sysco Brand across every customer type in our book of business, with independent customers being the area where we saw the greatest improvement, and that will continue into the rest of this year, which is one of the reasons why we had a strong gross margin performance in Q1.

Operator: Thank you. We will move next to Alex Slagle with Jefferies. Please go ahead.

Alex Slagle: Hey, thanks. Good morning, and congrats, Brandon, from me as well. Had a question on the national business. I missed if you provided a volume growth metric, but just questions more on the opportunity to further optimize how you attack the growth opportunities in these channels, especially the non-commercial, just to help offset some of the soft volumes in the chain business as you look out, leveraging tools, new tools you have, or shifting resources to accelerate growth in some of those higher potential segments of the business.

Kevin Hourican: Yeah, Alex, good morning. Thank you for the question. Contract business is half our business. It's really important. We don't directly call it national, but you can do the implied math. The implied math is 2.2% volume growth for contract business for Q1, which is solid. And the reason I say solid is because restaurants, national restaurants, are actually down year-over-year, and that's offset by really strong performance in what we call food service management, which is office buildings, big stadiums, college, and K-12 business. That all falls into that food service management sector. So strong performance in food service management, strong performance in hospitality. We're doing very well in the hospitality sector. We've got a renewed focus as a company on the selling strength capabilities within healthcare, strong partnerships in the healthcare GPO space, helping us profitably take share within healthcare. So 2.2% growth for the quarter. We're confident in our full year, and we've expanded our profitability in contract business as well by creating what I call win-win contract structures with our big customers, that if we work together and we create efficiencies, we share in some of those efficiencies with that customer, which motivates them to do that, and we are able to improve our profitability at the same time. So our contract sales leadership team is doing a terrific job. Thank you to that group. Alex, appreciate the question.

Operator: Thank you. We'll move next to John Ivankoe with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Ivankoe: Hi. Thank you. In my observations, one of what I think is some of the lowest hanging fruit at Restaurant Depot would be to improve customer-facing marketing and customer-facing technology, and those are obviously two areas Sysco has really put a lot of effort towards over the past several years, but also the past many years. Can you talk about, just from your perspective, Kevin, how big of an opportunity do you think that it is, and just remind me, do we have a vision that Restaurant Depot, Sysco really gets collapsed into one brand to kind of benefit from the marketing and customer-facing technology of the two businesses? Kevin Hourican: Yeah, John, great question. Appreciate it. First, let me just comment on where we are with the deal. As I said in my prepared remarks, we and Restaurant Depot have substantially complied to the second request. The FTC is doing their diligence. We have active conversations with them regularly. At this time, we are not aware of any concerns, and we are confident that the deal will get approved based on its factual merits. There is assortment expansion to each of the brands that we can create by leveraging each other's broad assortment. But John, what gets me most excited is the questions that you asked, the opportunity for revenue growth tied to what we call the better together thesis, and you hit on several of them. The Restaurant Depot team is excited to work with Sysco on customer-targeted personalization. We, as you know, because you said it, have invested heavily to create a personalized website. The AI360 capability that we have rides the rails of that hyper-personalization targeting logic. Restaurant Depot is a membership club.

Richard and his team know exactly what their customers are buying and not buying, and they are excited to partner with Sysco's tech team to bring forward customer-targeted promotional opportunities to engage more of their basket. Richard often talks about just adding one more case per visit is worth a lot, and we are going to work hard to do that. We will, of course, test these things. I call it pull, not push. It will be Richard and his team desiring these activities, and there is a tremendous amount of interest in this topic, specifically tied to data and technology and how we deploy it to actively engage the customers.

Brandon Sewell: Yeah, it's a somewhat tactical point, John, but one of the things that impresses us about Restaurant Depot is their data. Kevin Hourican: Thank you, Brandon. Last but not least, you asked about one brand. We will not change the brand of Restaurant Depot. That will stay on forever. The store is branded Restaurant Depot. You could have a delivery primary customer, ergo Sysco customer, who needs something in a hurry, leveraging the Restaurant Depot stores to do same-day delivery or will call pickup at a Restaurant Depot. That would be a Sysco delivery customer, but activated through the RD box. We believe there's big opportunity for that.

On the flip side, Restaurant Depot primary cash and carry customers at times grow and improve and strengthen their business and open a second or third door, and going to cash and carry becomes a challenge for them. We can create a model where we can predict that is occurring by the data that Brandon just referenced, and we can intervene and say, hey, we'd love to have Sysco deliver it to you once a week, and you can keep coming into the Restaurant Depot store to pick up your fresh products. That's an example of something we will build. But they're two different brands.

Because they're different customers, there's a cash and carry primary customer who chooses to go to the store to save money, and there's a delivery primary customer who likes delivery for the convenience and white glove service. Operator: Thank you. We will move next to Mark Carden with UBS. Please go ahead.

Mark Carden: Good morning. Thanks so much for taking the questions, and Brandon, congrats on the role. On your routing initiative, you talked about it being live in pilot regions. Kevin Hourican: All right, great, Mark. Thank you. Two-part question. I will do the routing part, Brandon will do the EPS part. I just wanted to be very clear on the routing project. That is a staged deployment throughout 2027. Think X sites per month being implemented. That project is on track. It is going well. There is a second project, which is what we are calling AI-infused routing, so improved simulation. We onboard a lot of new customers every single week, and doing that customer onboarding in a more efficient way right out of the gate, it is an easier-to-use software that will enable us to be more dynamic, and we are calling this customer-centric routing. So our best customers to get even tighter windows, smaller customers, working with them to have a little more flexibility so we can be efficient, so we can serve their business profitably. That is phase two.

Phase two will begin at the end of this fiscal year and is much more a fiscal 2028 financial contribution, which is why these AI profit impacts step up over time, $100 million this year and $500 million by the end of 2029. This project is one of the biggest projects in the hopper, and we have strong confidence in it. Again, I am really pleased with our routing team and our tech team for the good leadership they are displaying. Brandon, over to you to talk about Q2 and for your EPS.

Brandon Sewell: Yeah. Thank you, Mark, and thank you for the congratulations. If you look at it versus Q1, it will improve versus Q1. The phasing of our strategic sourcing and cost savings will enable that, and then Q3 and Q4 will continue to improve sequentially beyond Q2. So we will see a step up in Q2, we will see another step up in Q3 and Q4, and we will continue to execute with excellence.

Mark Carden: Great. Thanks so much and good luck, guys.

Operator: Thank you. We will take our final question from Sara Senatore with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Sara Senatore: Thank you very much. I wanted to go back to the commentary on, you mentioned on being thoughtful about making, what you are choosing to make the decisions about fuel headwind to ensure you keep the food affordable to your customers. So kind of sounds like you are passing through the deflation appropriately, but you are holding back on some of the fuel inflation. So I guess my interpretation is, you have big scale advantages, you have locked in your fuel better, I think, than some others. | Are you kind of using this as an opportunity to press your advantage to take volume?

Just because it seems like you are approaching how you think about fuel versus food inflation differently as you think about passing it through. Then, just related, it seems like the deflation kind of materialized very quickly, given that you issued the top-line guidance not that long ago. Is there anything that maybe needs to happen to change how you forecast inflation, or this was just unavoidable given the dairy oversupply, just even in short amount of time, couldn't have anticipated? Thank you.

Kevin Hourican: Yeah, very fair questions, Sara. Thank you. You had embedded in that product inflation, deflation, and fuel. Maybe we unpack the two. I'll start with product inflation. Brandon, maybe you take the fuel. First of all, we're constantly negotiating with our suppliers to get to the absolute best possible cost for Sysco, and then we contractually pass on our costs to the contract customers. Those are built into our contracts. For the street business, we dynamically price the street based on what's happening in the marketplace. If the marketplace understands that dairy is deflationary, we lower our price to match the fact that costs have come down and the marketplace has come down as well. We're very strategic, very thoughtful.

We price scrape our delivery competition on the regular. We talk to our suppliers about where we anticipate trends, and we change pricing for independent customers weekly because of the commodity fluctuations that happen in price. That's what I was alluding to in our prepared remarks. Yes, we passed on product deflation to independent and contract customers because that's the right thing to do. If our product cost comes down, our customers should benefit from that, and they did benefit from that in Q1. Your good question about, should we have seen the Q1 inflation? The category that was a surprise was dairy.

The oversupply of milk, and then it impacted the cheese market, was significant and happened quite rapidly, and that category behaved very differently than what we had expected. The second, which I didn't mention earlier, is while beef is still inflationary, the rate of inflation within beef is beginning to step down. That's good for end consumers, that is good for restaurants, but beef had been in the double-digit inflation for a long time. That is normalizing, and we are now expecting beef inflation for the rest of this year to be low single digits. Again, good for end restaurants, good for end consumers, but that is a big change from where it has been.

Your point on can we improve here? Yes, we can. We are leaning in hard to partner with our suppliers even stronger, leveraging some third-party tools to do ongoing rolling forecasting of commodity costs. We also have to respect that things change. Floods and droughts and pestilence occur, and it is a dynamic food environment. We do the best we can on forecasting inflation. Brandon was crystal clear. I'll just repeat it. We're seeing already in October back to inflation. We anticipate Q2 will be approximately 0.8%-1%, and we expect the full year now to be approximately what we guided on today's call.

Brandon, over to you for any additional comments on that, and then maybe you can talk about fuel and how we manage fuel through our P&L.

Brandon Sewell: Yeah, absolutely. I'll jump straight to fuel, and thank you for the question, Sara. With fuel, there are three components. The first is our contract customers and outbound. It is relatively formulaic. With that, there is a lag of roughly 90 days between contracts and what gets charged to the customer. On the local side, we as well intend and try to pass on the fuel costs that we're seeing when it comes to our retail component. Then, I mentioned this last time, on inbound, it's a little bit different because the suppliers sell us product. Obviously, we're not hedged on the inbound fuel. That is a place where we manage a balance between our customers and us internally.

With the increased cost of inbound and product, that's where there's a little bit of art and a little bit of science. All in all, I said initially that there was very little effect to operating income on fuel, thanks in large part to the hedges that we have in place and then to customer surcharges. We will continue to see that in Q2, and we will continue then to see it as well in 2H, as we are hedged 12 months out, and then we have smaller hedges that are 18 months out as well.

Operator: Thank you. At this time, we have reached the allotted time for questions. I will now turn the call back over to our presenters for any final or closing remarks.

Kevin Kim: Great. Thank you, Madison. Thank you, everybody, for joining us today and for your continued interest in Sysco. The team here is focused on the year to go. Should you have any follow-up questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to the investor relations team. Thank you very much.

Operator: This concludes today's meeting. We appreciate your time and participation. You may now disconnect. Thank you.

#3048. Mavericks vs. Kings Quoteboard: ‘We played their record … they played like pros.’

Nothing sucks the vibes out of the room quite like a loss to the winless Sacramento Kings on your home court. The Dallas Mavericks' (4-3) first win streak of the season is no more after Monday's 115-100 loss to the Kings (1-6) at American Airlines Center.

Kyrie Irving sat out under the "injury management" heading, which means rest, which means the coaching staff likely thought they could get the win without the man who scored a game-high 35 points in 35 minutes in Friday's 116-111 win over the Houston Rockets.

Twas not so. The Mavericks have zero other players on the roster who can do what Irving does for this team. Dribble the basketball, for one. Anyway, we move.

Here's what Mavs head coach Dusty May, center Daniel Gafford and backup guard Walter Clayton Jr. had to say in the postgame press conference about the ugly loss that saw the Mavericks shoot just 7-of-33 (21.2%) from 3-point range.

I want to credit Sacramento — that they were the more determined team tonight, the more prepared team and they came in and earned it. I want to give a lot of credit to their bench, those guys, their backups. Three wings, made a combined 12 threes for 36 points. So on nights like that, you've got to find ways to overcome your lack of shooting, and them shooting well, and we just weren't able to do that tonight.

A number of things. I thought once they got going, they were physical on the screens. We didn't put much pressure on the paint or the rim, and we were on our heels.

They loaded the paint, and there's a cadence to it where he's fanning out early, and we miss our first eight threes, and we thought several of them were good looks. And at that point, it fuels their fire to get to him even more in the paint, and they're collapsing on him. They're running second guy, third guy at him. I don't think our spacing, our relocations, were great as a whole, and we just didn't find any rhythm together.

Yeah, that's basketball. When you take [Walter Clayton Jr.] out of it, who made four of those seven, we were three for 28. And so it's tough to win basketball games like that. You have to have a lot of different areas, the steals, turnovers, getting to the line, which I thought we did a nice job getting to the line. You have to overcome that deficit in so many other areas, and we just weren't able to do it.

Win or a loss, we're going to look back at our process and just see, did we prepare the right way? Did we have the right game plan? What would we do differently next time? We'll have several learning experiences from this game. We do have a young team, and when it's not going well, we just kept stressing that everything's going poorly for us. But let's just find a way to hang around and get it till the end. But their shot-making prevented us from doing that. Those guys, they found great connection, especially in the fourth quarter, and found some match-ups, and I thought they played unselfish basketball.

I thought Caleb did a good job defensively. He made a shot. I don't think the lineup combinations offhand are the reason that they won tonight. We didn't do much well across the board, coaching, playing in any way. We just felt like he had a really good game last outing. His defense has been really, really sound for us.

He does so much for us, and making big shots, and calming us down. We haven't been able to answer runs very well. That's one area that he does. #3047. Crypto Market Today, Nov. 3: XRP and Zcash Defy Recent Weakness as Midterm Elections Take Center Stage

XRP and Zcash led Tuesday's crypto rebound as investors turned their attention to the U.S. midterm elections and what the results could mean for digital assets.

Bitcoin (BTC +1.28%) rose 1.49% to $77,828.21, Ethereum (ETH +1.72%) rose 1.98% to $2,293.77, and Solana (SOL +1.63%) rose 2.03% to $93.70. As of early evening on Nov. 3, the three coins were firmer even after a volatile session.

Broader financial markets regained some footing following several difficult sessions. The Nasdaq (NDAQ -1.52%) finished 0.83% higher, recovering alongside semiconductor stocks after concerns about artificial intelligence infrastructure spending and elevated valuations fueled a recent sell-off.

Bitcoin and crypto as a whole similarly rebounded from their intraday lows, although uncertainty surrounding the U.S. midterm elections and the broader economic outlook continues to present risks.

Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum funds were mostly higher alongside the coins, with iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT +1.62%) up 1.61%, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC +1.62%) up 1.62%, and iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA +2.05%) up 2.05%. This comes after consecutive days of spot outflows in Bitcoin ETFs, with $399 million in outflows on Monday, following $643 million on Friday.

Tuesday's recovery offered some relief for cryptocurrency investors, with XRP (XRP +2.54%) and Zcash (ZEC +6.55%) standing out among the stronger performers. Despite the positive ending to the day, many cryptocurrencies remain significantly down from their early fall highs and momentum remains fragile.

Attention now turns to the U.S. midterm elections, which could influence expectations around fiscal spending, artificial intelligence regulation, and digital asset policy. While the results may help resolve some uncertainty, investors will be watching how the political landscape affects broader financial markets and risk appetite heading into 2027.

#3046. CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt

CoreWeave's credit stress continued to spiral on Thursday amid a broader sell-off in AI-related names.

CoreWeave — a so-called neocloud company — has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to finance its AI infrastructure build-out. It's now facing a rebellion from stock and bond investors as concerns mount about AI overspending and debt levels.

Yields on CoreWeave debt have continued to climb, with the yield to maturity on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reaching 15.78%. Bond yields move inversely to prices. Meanwhile, the spread on its five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, at one point soared above 1,140 basis points. It last stood at nearly 1,038 bps — a 16% week-over-week jump and 164% higher than a year ago.

Credit concerns are spreading into AI equities too. CoreWeave's stock dropped during trading Thursday before recovering and closing 5.94% higher. The moved followed Wednesday's 15.5% nosedive.

Other neocloud stocks were under similar pressure. Nebius also sank before climbing higher to close 1.29% and and Iren ultimately ended the day down less than 1%.

Anxiety about AI overspending is also spreading. For instance, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices sold off following a big sell-off in South Korean chip stocks. Micron closed up 1.87%, while AMD fell 1.5%.

While AI debt worries have been rising steadily, investors have suddenly grown skittish about the underlying finances of companies borrowing heavily to buy chips, build data centers, and rent out computing power.

Coreweave's credit default swaps are one place to see that stress.

Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. The spread widening in CoreWeave's CDS means investors view the debt as riskier.

The market is "basically saying 'no mas' to AI debt without operating cash flow support," the Evercore ISI trading desk said.

A spread level of 1,000 basis points or above is generally a sign of credit distress, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

No one is questioning whether demand for CoreWeave's services is real, since the company has contracts with all the big hyperscalers, Nolan said. The question is whether the cash flows will ultimately arrive.

"It's obviously heavily negative free cash flow at the moment, and it needs that cash flow to arrive really to justify all the capex that it's spending," Nolan said.

CEO Mike Intrator dismissed the market moves on Wednesday, according to a memo obtained by CNBC.

"When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," he wrote. "We are confident in our backlog which more than supports all of our debt obligations."

The backlog is over $100 billion, with around two-thirds of it with investment-grade counterparts including Microsoft, Meta, IBM and Caterpillar, Deutsche Bank said in a note Thursday. The firm reiterated its buy-rating on the stock Wednesday, calling the dislocation a buying opportunity.

"The problem is this kind of concern can prove to be a self-fulfilling prophecy, and risks triggering broader issues in other AI-related names," said Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research.

Domino effects may already be happening. Oracle's five-year CDS spread also spiked this week. It was last at 282 basis points, a roughly 10% increase in one week.

"A downgrade from its BBB rating would risk pressuring IG-only investors into forced sales," Reid said.

#3044. Sabra Health (SBRA) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

SHOP is poised to outweigh skilled nursing for the first time in company history.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Sabra Health Care REIT, Inc. (SBRA +3.19%) reported a strategic shift toward its Senior Housing Operating Portfolio (SHOP), which is projected to reach 40% of the portfolio by year-end 2026 and 50% by the end of 2027. Management indicated that this transition will result in the senior housing portfolio outweighing the skilled nursing portfolio for the first time in company history. The company reported $747.2 million in year-to-date investments and an additional $425 million in awarded deals, which are expected to support a year-over-year earnings growth rate of 7% to 8% at the midpoint of 2026 guidance. Management is also focused on optimizing its skilled nursing segment through fair market rent resets upon lease expirations between 2027 and 2031. Leverage continues to trend downward, reaching 4.54x as the company utilizes its at-the-market equity program to fund a robust pipeline of value-add and stable assets.

#3043. Joe Lacob claims Yaxel Lendeborg's development has changed Warriors' outlook

Joe Lacob claims Yaxel Lendeborg's development has changed Warriors' outlook originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

Yaxel Lendeborg has exceeded just about everyone's expectations. Including his own.

Does that change the Warriors' outlook on the 2026-27 NBA season? Golden State owner Joe Lacob certainly believes so.

"I do," Lacob told 95.7 The Game's "Steiny & Guru" on Monday when asked if Lendeborg's immediate breakout has changed the team's outlook on the season. "Look, we've made our mistakes. Everyone makes mistakes, and we didn't get the draft exactly right, or maybe we didn't get the development right on a couple other higher draft choices in the past. Fine, criticize us for that, but the draft is hard guys.

"It is hard, and not everybody gets it. Some teams never get it right, and we got this one right. I was 100 percent sold that this was the guy we wanted in the draft, we were, not just me, and there were some other really good players in this draft. The only question was 'Would he get to No. 11?' And I was confident, actually that he would, because the NBA, I've been doing this a long time now, the NBA GMs just love their 18- and 19-year-olds. We've all been guilty of looking at 'There's great upside to some of these guys,' but this guy seemed like a champion, ready to play."

In eight games this season, Lendeborg is averaging 21.5 points, seven rebounds and 3.9 assists per game on 50-percent shooting from the field and 40 percent from 3-point range.

Not only has the rookie been an important piece to coach Steve Kerr's rotations, but he is Golden State's No. 2 scorer behind superstar Steph Curry. Lendeborg is putting up All-Star-caliber numbers early in his first NBA season for a team that is without its second scorer in Jimmy Butler, who still is working his way back from a torn ACL sustained last season and won't return until midseason.

When he does return, the Warriors could have a very formidable Big Three with Curry, Lendeborg and Butler.

"The amazing thing is, everything we thought he could be, he's come in and kind of exceeded that," Lacob added. "I think Steve has stated that. He's surprised Steve for sure. He doesn't have any weaknesses is what I would say."

Of course, it still is very early in the season, and Lendeborg almost certainly will experience plenty of highs and lows throughout the 82-game campaign. But the early returns on their first-round pick have Lacob and the Warriors very encouraged, and seemingly believing the team's ceiling might be higher than they initially thought it was.

#3041. Stock Market Today, Nov. 3: Grab Holdings Jumps 9% on Q3 Revenue Beat and Raised 2026 Outlook

On Nov. 3, 2026, shares of the Southeast Asian super-app climbed as profitability improved across all three core segments for the first time.

Grab Holdings (GRAB +9.09%), a Southeast Asian super-app for ride-hailing, delivery, and fintech services, closed at $3.12, up 9.09%. The stock rose after Grab reported Q3 revenue above estimates and raised its full-year 2026 outlook. Investors are watching whether the higher guidance and improved profitability extend the move. Trading volume reached 144.8M shares, coming in about 143% above its three-month average of 59.7M shares. Grab Holdings IPO'd in 2020 and has fallen 74% since going public.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.36%) rose 0.36% to 7,569, and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +0.83%) gained 0.83% to 25,372. In internet services: ride-hailing, delivery, and digital financial services, Uber Technologies (UBER -0.17%) closed at $66.61, down 0.15%, while DoorDash (DASH -3.55%) closed at $183.32, down 3.55%, as delivery-platform peers digested growth and margin updates.

Judging from its excellent Q3 earnings, Grab remains an intriguing, under-the-radar growth stock in my eyes. Management announced:

In addition to these promising figures, management raised full-year guidance to 25% sales growth and a 59% increase in adjusted EBITDA.

Though management also announced that the company's proposed acquisition of foodpanda's Taiwanese business for $600 million was canceled -- hitting GRAB with a $60 million breakup fee -- it was an otherwise great quarter all around.

Home to a net cash balance of roughly $6 billion, this fee is barely noticeable to the company, and Grab will likely continue to rely on acquisitions for future growth as it builds out the depth of services offered by its superapp.

Trading with a forward EV/EBITDA of 10 (using management's adjusted EBITDA guidance), Grab's high-growth figures and improving profitability are very reasonably priced.

Josh Kohn-Lindquist has positions in Uber Technologies. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends DoorDash. The Motley Fool recommends Grab and Uber Technologies. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

#3038. Takeaways from missing Marcus Smart in green

With Paul George sitting out the second night of a back-to-back and Boston playing their fifth game in eight nights, the Celtics snapped their five-game winning streak and lost to the Rockets 109-93. It was a demoralizing loss to a very good team, made only worse because of who was on the opposing team.

It's bittersweet to say, but it's all about Marcus Smart.

The former Celtic was everywhere on the floor. His stat line doesn't tell the story. He was 2-for-10 from the field; Alperen Segun paced all scorers with 26 on 12-of-15 shooting. He was just a +5 off the bench with the Rockets starters doing much of the damage in the game. With the ninth stingiest defense backing up the league's most efficient offense, the 6-1 Rockets have few weaknesses to take advantage of now that they have Fred Van Vleet and Smart at the point.

However, Boston was in this game. After Smart checked into the game at the 4:35 mark of the third quarter, the Celtics whittled down the lead to four. And then Smart happened.

During one stretch to start the fourth quarter, he was called for two consecutive dead ball defensive fouls that he followed up with back-to-back threes — the epitome of The Marcus Smart Experience that we know all so well. By the time he checked out midway through the final frame, Houston was up 100-82.

Since his departure in 2023, he's bounced around from four different teams, including a stint with Lakers last season. However, hooking up with Ime Udoka in Houston seems to be the right fit. For more insight to the former Celtics reunion with the Rockets, check out The Athletic's Will Guillory's profile on Smart and Udoka. Here's a snippet:

"There are some guys who have that defensive mentality, but it's rare to have a guy who comes into the game and impacts it the way he does on that side of the ball," Udoka said. "You saw it with Dillon, you saw it with Pat (Beverley). There are certain guys you have to prepare for because of what they do defensively. He's one of them."

"(Udoka's) mentality matched mine," Smart added. "He allowed me to be me without any persecution."

For the Celtics, they have several candidates that have filled in for Smart's Tommy Point contributions. Walsh's on-ball defense made him a starter earlier in the year. Scheierman chips in with the occasional hustle play or heady pass. Gonzalez often has the flair for the dramatic. But nobody has yet to solely take the mantle away from Marcus since his departure.

Last season, the Celtics were 7-11 when they shot under 30% from behind the arc. Before last night, they had endured a miserable game against the Nets in an overtime thriller and Sunday's brickfest over the Magic, but hitting just 12-of-42 in Houston just wasn't enough against an elite Rockets team.

Tatum made just one of his 7 triples. Pritchard and Hauser missed all five of their attempts each. The only bright spot was Garza's 4-for-7 clip.

Maybe it was a lack of legs in the second night of a back-to-back or missing Paul George's catch-and-shoot prowess on the wing, but stinkers like this are going to happen every sixth game or so. As long as they're figuring out other ways to win, it shouldn't be too big of an issue.

Once a Celtic, always a Celtic. Love and trust, Smarty.

"To be honest, I gotta figure it out soon. I don't know." — Mitchell Robinson on his impact on the offensive boards

After missing the previous game against the Magic, Robinson was replaced by Neemias Queta in the starting lineup. Soon after coming off the bench, he jammed his thumb and went to the locker room for a brief stint in the second quarter. He did make both of his looks from the field, but his one offensive board on the night was just his fifth in three games. That was supposed to be his calling card.

Head coach Joe Mazzulla said after the loss that Robinson's decreased impact is partly because they have him playmaking by setting screens further away from the rim, but after leading the league last season with 7.7 offensive rebounds per 36 minutes, it's been a disappointing start for the Celtics' key free agent signing of the summer.

The team will return home to TD Garden to host the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday at 7:30 pm EST before heading back out on the road for four games in Charlotte, Milwaukee, Philadelphia, and Toronto.
